 What changes to look for with Medicare open enrollment By Cassidy Williams Published : Oct. 29, 2026 at 6:32 PM EDT | Updated : 13 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google (WFSB) - Medicare open enrollment is going on right now. So, what changes should you look for?
 When picking a plan, the monthly payment, or premium, is an important number to consider. But, it should not be the only thing behind your decision.
 “So oftentimes what we’ll see is people shopping on the basis of the premium. And oftentimes they’re looking for the lowest premium, which makes a lot of sense, but the reality is sometimes you may be paying a higher premium and your total costs, meaning your premium plus your out-of-pocket costs, is actually lower because it provides better coverage,” said Leigh Purvis, Prescription Drug Policy Principal, AARP Public Policy Institute.
 She says you should also look at things like your out of pocket maximum and how much your prescriptions will cost.
 She added that one thing changing next year is the deductible for Medicare Part D, which covers prescription drugs.
 The deductible is now a $700 maximum, up from $615. The out of pocket maximum has also jumped from $2,100 to $2,400.
 “I think it’s really important for people to keep in mind how many different ways you can see those plans changing. Whether it is your deductibles, your out-of-pocket limits, what services are covered, how much you have to pay for those services, and whether the plan is offered at all,” said Purvis.
 If you are looking for someone to help you decide, she recommends using the state health insurance assistance program, or SHIP.
 “You can locate the one closest to you at SHIPhelp.org. And they’re very good at providing objective, individualized assistance,” she explained.
 Medicare open enrollment runs through December 7th.
